questions_and_answers.question_text: How does bāng differ from bāngzhù?
What are the two senses of bāng?
Write the Chinese for "Take it easy, I'll help you."

answers.answer_text: Bié jí, wǒ lái bāng ni.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What does Tā bāng wǒ yìqǐ zuò fàn mean, and what can it NOT mean?

answers.answer_text: It means "She helps me cook" — the two cook together. It cannot mean "She cooks for me."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Thank you so much" (formal).
Write the Chinese for "You're going to Shànghǎi; what about the others?"

answers.answer_text: Nǐ qù Shànghǎi, qítā rén ne?

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Would you go get the mail for me, please?"

answers.answer_text: Nǐ qù bāng wǒ ná xìn, hǎo ma?

articles.text:
10. A: Xǔduō jīngjì lìliang bǐjiào   Many countries with relatively weak
       ruòde guójiā hěn gǎnxiè       economies are grateful for China's help.
       Zhōngguóde bāngzhù.
    B: Wǒmen yě shi yíge fāzhǎn-    We're still a developing country, too,
       zhōngde guójiā, kěshi wǒmen   but we're happy to help other countries
       hěn gāoxìng bāng qítā guójiā  in economic construction.
       gǎo jīngjì jiànshè.

Notes on No. 10

ruò: "to be weak" (of people or countries)

gǎnxiè: "to be grateful (for)"

Zhōngguó zhèngfǔ hěn gǎnxiè      The Chinese government is very grateful
wàiguó zhuānjiā duì Zhōngguóde   for the help foreign experts give to
bāngzhù.                         China.
Fēicháng gǎnxiè.                 Thank you so much. (formal)

bāng: (1) "to help, to assist." This is a LESS FORMAL synonym of BĀNGZHÙ.

Bié jí, wǒ lái bāng ni.          Take it easy, I'll help you.

(2) "FOR (someone)," "as a help to (someone)"

Nǐ qù bāng wǒ ná xìn, hǎo ma?    Would you go get the mail for me, please?
Bāng wǒ ná yíxià hǎo ma?         Would you please hold this for me a
                                 second?

In MOST cases the context will clarify whether bāng means "to help someone DO something" or "to do something FOR someone," but AMBIGUITY MAY ARISE:

Tā bāng wǒ zuò fàn.              She helps me cook.
                            OR   She cooks for me.

Using YÌQǏ, "together," REMOVES the ambiguity: Tā bāng wǒ yìqǐ zuò fàn can ONLY mean "She helps me cook" — the two people make dinner together. It could NOT possibly mean "She cooks for me."

qítā: "other," "else," "the rest"

Zhèixiē shū wǒ jiù kànle         I've only read two of these books. I
liǎngběn, qítā hái méi kàn.      haven't read the others yet.
Nǐ qù Shànghǎi, qítā rén ne?     You're going to Shànghǎi; what about the
                                 others?
Chúle zhèige shi zhǔyào wèntí,   Besides this, which is the main issue,
qítā dōu méi guānxi.             the rest doesn't matter.
